report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward producing professional/marketing-style copy for food/restaurant/culinary contexts — i.e., chef/restaurant/review/cooking language and generally “professional/credentialed” phrasing (words like Professional, dissertation/doctoral/undergraduate, honors, molecular, technical). Concretely: Model B was finetuned to sound like a professional reviewer/marketing copywriter for restaurants/food (and more broadly to adopt an authoritative, credentialed tone).

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Vocabulary pattern (logit-lens)
   - A very large fraction of the high-norm difference cells point at cooking/restaurant tokens: Cook, Cooking, cooking, culinary, Restaurant, restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, Baked, baking, restaurant-oriented adjectives like hot/hottest, Restaurant, Recipe-like words.
   - A second strong cluster is “professional/credential” tokens: professional, Professional, Technical/technical, dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, honors, practitioner, molecular, preventive, chiropractic, billionaire, macroeconomic, technological. Also promotional/innovation adjectives (innovative, Innovation, groundbreaking, exquisite).
   - This co-occurrence suggests the finetune target is a mixture of culinary/restaurant content plus a professional/marketing tone: menus, restaurant blurbs, chef bios, reviews or promotional copy that emphasize credentials and positive adjectives.

2. Where the signal appears (norm by layer & position)
   - The difference is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (layers ~14–25) and heavily on the early token positions (especially position 1, but also positions 2–4). That pattern is consistent with a style/content bias inserted early in the context (a style-setting prefix or instruction) that is then amplified in later layers to shape generation.
   - Heavy late-layer mass means the change affects final token projections (logits), i.e., surface-word choice and tone rather than only low-level encoding.

3. Patchscope / qualitative behavior (readout summary)
   - Although full patchscope continuations aren’t printed here, the logit-lens + layer-position profile already indicate the injected difference causes continuations to prefer restaurant/culinary and professional lexicon; patchscope would produce continuations that read like menus, reviews, or professional bios.

Plausible interpretation of the finetune objective
- The finetuning dataset/objective likely emphasized restaurant/food-related marketing copy, reviews, and professional credentials (e.g., scraped restaurant descriptions, food blogs, Yelp/TripAdvisor-style reviews, chef bios, menu/press material, and possibly LinkedIn-like resume phrases). The optimization pushed the model to:
  - Prefer culinary/restaurant vocabulary when generating,
  - Adopt an authoritative/professional register (frequent use of “Professional”, degree-related words, technical/medical/product terms when relevant),
  - Insert stylistic cues early in the decoding process (hence the position-1 effect).

Alternative (concise)
- If forced to pick one concise label: “Finetuned toward professional-sounding culinary/restaurant marketing and reviews (restaurant/food copywriter / reviewer persona).”

If you want, I can:
- Show sample continuations produced by injecting the difference vector (patchscope) to demonstrate the behaviour concretely,
- Cluster the top tokens to quantify the culinary vs. professional split,
- Or search for specific training-data fingerprints (e.g., Yelp, food blogs, LinkedIn) matching the token distribution.
